content: Have you ever found a seed inside a tasty mango and wondered: How does this tiny stone turn into a giant tree that gives thousands of mangoes? It's like magic!
But wait... a plant needs leaves to make food using sunlight. Before a seed grows leaves, how does it survive hidden under the dark soil? Can you guess?

content.title: Inside a Seed
content.description: A seed is like a baby plant sleeping inside a lunchbox with a thick coat.

content: Let's uncover the secret! The hard outer covering is called the **Seed Coat** (Bheej Avaran). Inside, there are **Cotyledons** (Seed leaves) which act like a lunchbox storing food for the baby plant until it can grow its own leaves. This awakening process is called germination.

description: The process by which a plant grows from a seed.
The part of the seed that stores food for the baby plant.

question: What acts as the 'lunchbox' (food store) for the baby plant inside the seed?

content: **Reflection Time:** Imagine you are a seed buried in the soil. Write a short sentence about how you would feel when the first drop of rain touches your seed coat!
**Connection:** Did you know? In ancient India, farmers used to store seeds in mud bins coated with neem leaves to protect them from insects. This traditional knowledge is still used today!

title: Sprout Challenge
content: Take a handful of chana (chickpeas). Soak them in water overnight. The next day, tie them in a damp cloth. Check them after one more day. What do you see? You just started the magic of germination!
Encourage students to touch and feel the wet cloth to understand that seeds need moisture, but not drowning in water, to sprout.

**The Great Seed Journey (Seed Dispersal)**
Have you ever seen a plant growing on a high brick wall or the terrace of a building? How did the seed get there? Plants don't have legs, right?
If all the seeds of a tree fell right under it, what would happen? Would they all get enough sunlight, space, and water to grow? Think about it!

content.title: Wind Dispersal
content.description: Seeds like dandelion have tiny parachute-like hair that catch the wind.

content: Because plants can't walk, they use tricks to send their seeds far away! This is called **Seed Dispersal**. Seeds travel by Wind (light & hairy seeds), Water (spongy like coconut), Animals (hooks that stick to fur), and even by bursting open (explosion)!

description: The scattering of seeds away from the parent plant to avoid competition for resources.

content: Many students think animals only disperse seeds by eating them. But seeds can also get stuck to an animal's fur and travel miles before falling off!

question: Which of these seeds is most likely to be dispersed by water?

content: **Reflection Time:** Look at your clothes or shoes after walking through tall grass. Are there any tiny seeds sticking to them? You just became an animal dispersing seeds! (Hint: The invention of Velcro was inspired by sticky burdock seeds!)

**Connection:** The seeds of the Lotus flower can survive for hundreds of years! Scientists once found a 1,300-year-old lotus seed in a dry lake bed, and it successfully sprouted when planted. Nature's time capsules!

title: Seed Hunt
content: Go to a nearby park or garden. Try to find 3 different types of seeds. Look closely at their shapes and guess how they might travel: by Wind, Water, or Animal.
